lines.trans: Wait—look at the faint blue lines drawn along the outer edges of each card!
Turn them face up on the flat bench slat like four tiles of one square...
Card One top left, Card Two top right, Card Three bottom left, Card Four bottom right!
Incredible! Together the four backs form a bird-eye drawing of Jasmine Courtyard!
There is our courtyard tree, there are the arched windows of Room Nine...
And look up on the second-floor wooden courtyard balcony—a bright red painted star!
Why did the mapmaker paint a red star on our upstairs courtyard balcony?!
Perhaps the small wax-sealed envelope in your pocket has the answer, Nour!
We walked every clue honestly—even Rami and his extra circle—so let us open it!

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: The number four, used with feminine nouns.

examples.trans: I have four cars.

examples.text: ضل أربع ساعات على موعد الطيارة.
examples.trans: There are four hours left until the flight time.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: I bought four books.
The guests arrived at four in the afternoon.

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The color of my car is blue.

examples.text: السما اليوم لونها أزرق صافي وما في غيم.
examples.trans: The sky today is a clear blue and there are no clouds.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The number two. Often pronounced 'tnēn' in Jordanian.

examples.trans: I have two children.

examples.text: طلبنا فنجانين قهوة وكاستين شاي للاثنين.
examples.trans: We ordered two cups of coffee and two glasses of tea for the two of us.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait just a minute.

examples.text: استنى شوي، أنا نازل معك هسه!
examples.trans: Wait a second—I'm coming down with you right now!

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: The man who I saw yesterday.

examples.text: هذا المحل اللي اشترينا منه الكنافة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: This is the shop where we bought the kunafa last week.

meanings.note: After a plural verb, بعض means 'each other' (بننادي بعض 'we call each other').

examples.trans: We call each other by first name here.

examples.text: ما حكينا مع بعض من زمان.
examples.trans: We have not spoken with each other in a long time.

meanings.note: Plural of بلاطة, the everyday Arabic word for a paving stone or floor tile.

examples.text: في بلاطة مكسورة عند مدخل الحوش لازم نبدلها.
examples.trans: There is a cracked tile at the courtyard entrance that we need to replace.

examples.text: بلاطات الحوش الحجرية بتضل باردة حتى بالصيف.
examples.trans: The stone courtyard flagstones stay cool even in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian noun for a balcony or veranda.

examples.text: شربنا القهوة عالبلكونة الخشب الطابق التاني.
examples.trans: We drank coffee on the wooden balcony on the second floor.
The balcony of Jasmine House overlooks the courtyard.

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian/Levantine modal adverb expressing hope or possibility.

examples.text: بلكي نلاقي الكرت التاني جوا العلبة.
examples.trans: Maybe we will find the second card inside the tin.

examples.text: استنى شوي، بلكي سلمى ترجع بعد دقايق.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, perhaps Salma will come back in a few minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.trans: My brother's car is broken.
Where is the key belonging to the kitchen cupboard?

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: The cat is hiding under the table.

examples.text: لقينا البطاقة التانية تحت الصحن الأبيض.
examples.trans: We found the second card under the white plate.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: I have nine books on the shelf.

examples.text: الساعة تسعة الصبح رح نلتقي عند النافورة.
examples.trans: At nine in the morning we will meet by the fountain.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Count to ten: one, two, three.

examples.text: رتبنا الصحون واحد تنين تلاتة عالطاولة.
examples.trans: We lined up the plates one, two, three on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine noun for an answer or musical response (plural: أجوبة).

examples.trans: A breath first and a second answer on the key.
We are waiting for an answer from City Hall tomorrow.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جيب.

examples.trans: Put the key in the coat pocket.
The paper is in my right pocket.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for the rim of a tin or the edge of a paving stone (الحافة الشمالية 'the north edge'). Plural: حواف.

examples.trans: We wrapped white tape around the rim of the tin.
Lower the north edge first gently.

meanings.note: Used to mean 'even' (e.g., even he went) or 'until' (e.g., until tomorrow).

examples.text: ما أكلت ولا إشي، حتى تفاحة.
examples.trans: I didn't eat anything, not even an apple.

examples.text: ما فتحنا الصندوق حتى قرأنا كل البطاقات.
examples.trans: We did not open the box until we read all the cards.

meanings.note: Describes outer shutters, doors, or walls facing the courtyard or street.

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش الخارجي بلون أخضر دافي.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the outside shutters a warm green.

examples.text: الباب الخارجي بيفتح مباشرة على شارع الياسمين.
examples.trans: The exterior gate opens straight onto Jasmine Street.

meanings.note: Standard word for a geographical or digital map.

examples.text: افتح الخريطة على التلفون عشان ما نضيع.
examples.trans: Open the map on the phone so we don't get lost.
We followed the blue lines on the old map.

meanings.note: Feminine word derived from خشب ('wood'), agreeing with عدة.

examples.text: عندي عدة خشبية صغيرة بصلّح فيها الكراسي.
examples.trans: I have a small wooden toolkit I use to fix the chairs.

examples.text: الباب الخشبي القديم بيعطي البيت دفا وروح.
examples.trans: The old wooden door gives the house warmth and character.

meanings.note: Can mean a physical line, a phone line, a bus route, or handwriting.

examples.trans: There is no coverage, the line is disconnecting.

examples.text: رسمنا خط مستقيم بالمسطرة على الورقة.
examples.trans: We drew a straight line with the ruler on the sheet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Can mean evidence, proof, or a guide (both a person and a guidebook).

examples.trans: Do you have evidence for what you're saying?

examples.text: هادا الرقم الصغير هو أول دليل للوصول للكنز.
examples.trans: This small number is the first clue for reaching the treasure.

meanings.note: Intensive occupation noun from رسم ('draw/paint'). رسام خرايط means 'mapmaker/cartographer'.

examples.text: رسام الخرايط قعد على طاولة واحد.
examples.trans: The mapmaker sat down at table one.

examples.text: هاد الرسام عمل لوحة رائعة للشارع.
examples.trans: This artist made a wonderful painting of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for drawing a picture, a map or a plan.

examples.trans: He drew me a map to the shop on a piece of paper.

examples.text: بنتي بترسم بيوت وشجر كل يوم.
examples.trans: My daughter draws houses and trees every day.

meanings.note: A noun referring to a single drawing, illustration, or painting.

examples.trans: This drawing is very beautiful.

examples.text: في رسمة صغيرة لورقة زيزفون على الهامش.
examples.trans: There is a small drawing of a linden leaf in the margin.

meanings.note: Colloquial active participle of زاد (to increase), pronounced zaayid without medial hamza.

examples.text: في عسل زايد بالمرطبان، خليه للكيكة التانية.
examples.trans: There is extra honey in the jar; save it for the second cake.

examples.text: الكلام الزايد ما إله داعي هلق.
examples.trans: Extra talk is unnecessary right now.

meanings.note: Extremely common Levantine preposition meaning 'like' or 'similar to'.

examples.trans: You are like my brother.

examples.text: ريحة الزيزفون زي ريحة الربيع بالقرية.
examples.trans: The scent of linden is like the scent of spring in the village.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a tree.

examples.trans: We planted an olive tree in the garden.

examples.text: قعدنا تحت شجرة الزيزفون الكبيرة بالساحة.
examples.trans: We sat under the big linden tree in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Abstract noun meaning honour or prestige, also appearing in polite expressions like إلنا الشرف (the honour is ours).

examples.trans: Your visit to our house is a great honour for us.

examples.text: أعطانا كلمة شرف إنه يحفظ السر.
examples.trans: He gave us his word of honour to keep the secret.

meanings.note: Collective noun for wax or candles.

examples.text: ذوبنا شمع عشان نعمل شكل جديد.
examples.trans: We melted wax to make a new shape.

examples.text: ختموا المغلف بشمع أحمر وعليه طابع قديم.
examples.trans: They sealed the envelope with red wax and an old stamp.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.text: عندي أخ صغير عمره خمس سنين.
examples.trans: I have a young brother who is five years old.

examples.text: في مفتاح نحاس صغير مخبي تحت الورقة.
examples.trans: There is a small brass key hidden under the sheet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: The bedroom is very spacious.

examples.text: غرفة المكتبة هادية ومليانة كتب خرائط.
examples.trans: The library room is quiet and full of atlases.

meanings.note: Idiomatic Arabic colour modifier (أصفر فاقع 'bright lemon yellow', أخضر فاقع 'vivid green').

examples.text: لون الليمون الأصفر الفاقع طالع حلو جنب الأخضر.
examples.trans: The bright lemon-yellow colour looks great next to the green.

examples.text: ما بدنا لون فاقع، بدنا أخضر هادي متل الغابة.
examples.trans: We don't want a flashy shade—we want a calm forest green.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The book is on top of the table.

examples.text: الخريطة معلقة فوق الرف الخشبي بالمكتبة.
examples.trans: The map is hanging above the wooden shelf in the library.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There are many people in the market.

examples.text: في تلات بطاقات ملونة جوا الظرف الكبير.
examples.trans: There are three coloured cards inside the big envelope.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قلوب.

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast with joy!
Welcome from the bottom of my heart.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: All people love summer.

examples.text: كل بطاقة بالعلبة بتحكي عن نبتة عطرية مختلفة.
examples.trans: Every card in the tin talks about a different aromatic plant.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Used in Jordan to mean a wrap or a sandwich (e.g. falafel or shawarma), or a turn in the road.

examples.trans: I want a falafel sandwich with fries.

examples.text: أخذنا لفة سريعة بالسوق واشترينا زعتر وفستق.
examples.trans: We took a quick stroll around the market and bought thyme and pistachios.

meanings.note: Compound directional adverb combining لـ (toward) and فوق (above); opposite of لتحت.

examples.text: اطلع لفوق عالطابق التاني بتلاقي الغرفة.
examples.trans: Go upstairs to the second floor and you will find the room.
The red arrow on the map points upwards.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: The standard colloquial interrogative for 'why' in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Why were you late to work today?

examples.text: ليش الحبر على طرف الورقة مبين أغمق من النص؟
examples.trans: Why does the ink at the edge of the sheet look darker than the middle?

meanings.note: Passive participle of ختم (to stamp/seal), modifying مغلف in definiteness and gender.

examples.text: وصل مغلّف مختوم من البلدية اليوم الصبح.
examples.trans: A stamped envelope from the municipality arrived this morning.

examples.text: لازم الورقة تكون مختومة بختم رسمي عشان يقبلوها.
examples.trans: The paper has to be stamped with an official seal for them to accept it.

meanings.note: Denotes a square shape or a square area in geometry or real-world objects.

examples.trans: Draw a square on the paper.

examples.text: رسمنا مربع صغير جنب كل رقم عالورقة.
examples.trans: We drew a small square next to each number on the sheet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مرسومة, plural: مرسومين).

examples.text: في مفتاح دهبي مرسوم فوق الباب.
examples.trans: There is a golden key painted above the door.
The map is drawn by hand.

meanings.note: Used for flat surfaces like roofs or fields.

examples.trans: The roof of the house is flat.

examples.text: فردنا العجينة على لوح خشب مسطح ونضيف.
examples.trans: We rolled the dough out on a clean, flat wooden board.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: I am not upset with you.

examples.text: هادا المفتاح مش للباب الرئيسي، هادا للخزانة.
examples.trans: This key is not for the main door; this one is for the cupboard.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: Standalone معقول! is a classic Jordanian exclamation of amazed disbelief ('No way! / Could it really be?!').

examples.text: معقول! قطار جدي الخشب لسا موجود!
examples.trans: Could it be! Grandfather's wooden train is still around!
The price is reasonable and fair for everyone.

meanings.note: Refers to a paper envelope used for letters or documents.

examples.trans: I put the money in an envelope.

examples.text: حطينا البطاقات كلها جوا مغلف ورق بني.
examples.trans: We put all the cards inside a brown paper envelope.

meanings.note: Noun of place from ق-ع-د ('to sit'); names the seat of a chair or a garden bench.

examples.text: ارفع مقعد الكرسي شوي عشان يطوي معك.
examples.trans: Lift the chair seat slightly so it folds for you.

examples.text: في مقعد خشب طويل تحت شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: There is a long wooden bench under the courtyard tree.

meanings.note: From قوس, an arch or bow: arched windows are شبابيك مقوسة.

examples.trans: The mosque's door is arched and tall.
They have old arched windows.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Used for celestial stars, geometric shapes, or famous celebrities.

examples.trans: The sky is full of stars today.

examples.text: رسموا نجمة صغيرة بالحبر الأحمر جنب الرقم سبعة.
examples.trans: They drew a small star in red ink beside the number seven.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'she' or 'it' (feminine).

examples.trans: Take a piece of bread while it is hot.
Family is what remains.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: There is someone asking about you.

examples.text: اشتريت كتاب واحد بس من المعرض لأنه كان غالي.
examples.trans: I bought just one book from the fair because it was expensive.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Direction noun synonymous with شمال (left) in urban speech; frequently used as عاليسار (on the left).

examples.text: المكتبة موجودة على جهة اليسار بعد القوس.
examples.trans: The library is on the left side right after the arch.

examples.text: لفوا يسار عند النافورة بتلاقوا الممر.
examples.trans: Turn left at the fountain and you will find the passage.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.
